originalAlarm.description: Value stored to 'irq' during its initialization is never read

presenceCondition:
(or (and CONFIG_TWL4030_CORE (not CONFIG_IRQ_DOMAIN) CONFIG_OF_IRQ)
    (and CONFIG_TWL4030_CORE CONFIG_IRQ_DOMAIN (not CONFIG_OF_IRQ))
    (and CONFIG_TWL4030_CORE CONFIG_IRQ_DOMAIN CONFIG_OF_IRQ)
    (and (not CONFIG_TWL4030_CORE) CONFIG_IRQ_DOMAIN CONFIG_OF_IRQ)
    (and (not CONFIG_TWL4030_CORE) CONFIG_IRQ_DOMAIN (not CONFIG_OF_IRQ))
    (and CONFIG_TWL4030_CORE (not CONFIG_IRQ_DOMAIN) (not CONFIG_OF_IRQ)))
model:
(define-fun CONFIG_TWL4030_CORE () Bool
  true)
(define-fun CONFIG_IRQ_DOMAIN () Bool
  false)
(define-fun CONFIG_OF_IRQ () Bool
  false)
reasoning: FALSE POSITIVE: The alarm reports 'irq' (int irq = *ops at line 12 in irq_domain_add()) as a dead store — irq is initialized but never subsequently used in the simplified file. In the real Linux kernel irq_domain_add() code, the dereferenced ops value is actively used for IRQ domain operations. The simplified file stripped those subsequent uses, making irq appear as a dead store. This is a simplification artifact. The known vbdb bug (NullDereference: ops is NULL when !OF_IRQ) is a separate issue from this dead store alarm.
